group.passage:
Pikas, rodent-like creatures belonging to the family Ochotonidae within the order Lagomorpha, are small, mountain-dwelling mammals found in Asia and North America. Measuring approximately 15 centimeters in length and weighing between 125 and 200 grams, they are characterized by their dark bead-like eyes, rounded ears, lack of an external tail, and soft, dense fur. Unlike their lagomorph relatives—rabbits and hares, pikas have shorter hind limbs, resulting in a brisk scurry rather than bounding leaps when they move around.
Adapted to cold, alpine environments, pikas inhabit rocky slopes and meadows at elevations reaching up to 6,000 meters. They are active in the daytime, especially during cooler parts of the day. Notably, pikas do not hibernate, and they prepare for winter by creating “haypiles”—collections of dried vegetation such as grasses, flowers, and twigs—which they store under rocks or in crevices for sustenance during the colder months. Their diet primarily consists of various plant materials, including leaves, stems, seeds, and occasionally bark. Pikas exhibit coprophagy, which is a common trait among lagomorphs. They have two types of droppings: hard pellets and soft cecotropes, and they consume the latter once again to extract additional nutrients.
Pikas’ reproductive and social behaviors have also fascinated scientists. Reproduction occurs in the spring, with females typically producing two to six offspring per litter after carrying them for about 30 days. The young are born altricial—blind and nearly hairless—but grow rapidly, reaching adult size within 40 to 50 days. Social structures among pikas vary by species and habitat. Rock-dwelling species tend to be solitary and territorial, using vocalizations to communicate and defend their areas. In contrast, burrowing species often live in family groups, exhibiting more social behaviors.
Pikas are not just survivors of high-altitude life—they are vital indicators of ecosystem health. Their sensitivity to temperature changes makes them early warning systems for climate shifts, particularly in alpine regions. As temperatures rise, pikas are forced to retreat to higher elevations or face local extinction, highlighting the urgency of preserving their habitats. Humans need to put more effort into conservation to ensure that these remarkable creatures continue to thrive in their mountainous homes.

figures.label: 第1題選項(A)–(D)圖片
figures.caption: 第1題：四個選項各為一張黑白動物插圖
figures.description: 第1題的四個選項都是灰階線條插圖，各畫一隻小型哺乳動物，題目要選出最像鼠兔（pika）的一張。(A) 是一隻兔子，耳朵又長又尖、直立，蹲坐，後腳長而大，身後有短尾巴；(B) 是一隻以細長後腿直立站著的小動物，耳朵很大很圓、身形瘦長，前腳縮在胸前，像沙鼠或跳鼠；(C) 是一隻圓滾滾、四肢短小、四腳著地的小動物，耳朵小而圓、眼睛是黑色小珠子、有鬍鬚，沒有外露的尾巴，毛皮蓬鬆；(D) 是一隻胖嘟嘟的小動物，坐著、前掌在胸前合攏，耳朵圓、眼睛瞇起，背部毛色深、腹部淺，像倉鼠。
rows: 兔子：長而尖的直立耳朵、後腳長大、有短尾巴，蹲坐
以細長後腿直立的小動物：大圓耳、身形瘦長，前腳縮在胸前（像沙鼠／跳鼠）
圓滾滾的小動物：耳朵小而圓、黑珠眼、有鬍鬚、四肢短、無外露尾巴，四腳著地趴伏
胖嘟嘟的小動物：坐著、前掌合攏、圓耳、瞇眼，背深腹淺（像倉鼠）

questions.stem: Which of the following pictures best depicts a pika?

options.A: ［圖］一隻兔子：一對又長又尖、直立的大耳朵，蹲坐著，後腳長而大，身後有一小撮短尾巴。
options.B: ［圖］一隻用兩條細長後腿直立站著的小動物：一對很大的圓耳朵，身形瘦長，前腳縮在胸前，像沙鼠或跳鼠。
options.C: ［圖］一隻圓滾滾的小動物：四肢短小、四腳著地趴伏著，耳朵小而圓，眼睛是黑色小圓珠，有鬍鬚，看不到外露的尾巴，毛皮蓬鬆。
options.D: ［圖］一隻胖嘟嘟的小動物：坐著、前掌在胸前合攏，耳朵圓，眼睛瞇成一條線，背部毛色較深、腹部較淺，像倉鼠。

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements about pikas is true?

options.A: Though pikas do not hibernate, they need little food or water for the winter.
options.B: Some pikas live alone and avoid others, while others form a close bond with family.
options.C: Pikas feed on hard pellets and soft cecotropes, both of which are nutritious.
options.D: Small and weak as they may look, newborn pikas can leave their mothers right after birth.

questions.stem: What does the author imply in the last paragraph?

options.A: It has been a hard time for pikas to get used to warmer weather conditions.
options.B: Pikas will be much more likely to survive in a nature reserve than in the wild.
options.C: Despite the threat of climate change, pikas have managed to survive and thrive.
options.D: Pikas are on the verge of extinction due to the loss of their intuitive sensitivity.
